learning_objective: 🎯 Learn to solve mathematical conditions where things aren't exactly equal, graph the limits on number lines, and shade acceptable solution regions on a 2D plane!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An equation says two things are equal ($x = 5$). An inequality says one thing is greater or less than another ($x < 5$ or $x \geq 5$). Strict inequalities use $<$ or $>$, while Slack inequalities include the possibility of being equal ($\leq$ or $\geq$).

You can add, subtract, multiply, and divide inequalities just like normal equations, WITH ONE HUGE EXCEPTION: If you multiply or divide both sides by a NEGATIVE number, the inequality sign MUST FLIP. (e.g., $-2x < 6$ becomes $x > -3$).

When the solution is in one variable, we show it on a number line. Use an open circle ($\circ$) for $<$ or $>$ (number not included), and a solid dark circle ($\bullet$) for $\leq$ or $\geq$ (number included).

For equations like $2x + 3y \leq 6$, first graph it as a straight line $2x + 3y = 6$. Then, pick a test point (usually $(0,0)$). If $(0,0)$ makes the inequality true, shade the side of the line containing $(0,0)$. That shaded area is your Solution Region!

fun_activity.title: 🛒 The Budget Shopper
fun_activity.instructions: You have ₹500. A burger costs ₹100 ($x$) and a soda costs ₹50 ($y$). The inequality is $100x + 50y \leq 500$. You can't buy negative items, so $x \geq 0, y \geq 0$. Plot this on a graph and shade the triangle. Every whole-number coordinate inside that shaded triangle is a valid combo you can buy!

exam_tips: 📌 Forgetting to FLIP the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is the #1 mistake students make. Put a star next to this rule in your notes!
📌 When graphing $x < 2$ or $y > 3$ on a 2D plane, ALWAYS draw a dotted/dashed line. For $\leq$ or $\geq$, draw a solid continuous line.
📌 In system of inequalities graphs, the final answer is ONLY the region where ALL shaded areas intersect/overlap.
quick_recap: ⭐ The solution of a linear inequality in one variable is an interval (e.g., $(-\infty, 5]$).
⭐ A straight line divides the Cartesian plane into two parts called 'half-planes'.
⭐ The test-point method (plugging in $x=0, y=0$) is the fastest way to determine which half-plane to shade.
